distinguishing_features: Physical insertion of thin conductive epoxy interlayers at predetermined radial positions within the bushing potting.
Interlayers form equipotential grading screens that divide voltage among dielectric sections to reduce radial field peaks.
Manufacturing-time implementation via multiple potting injections and ultrasonic placement verification rather than online leakage-current/temperature diagnostics.
Direct bench validation of surface electric-field gradient reduction under DC stress.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Mitigating local electric-field enhancement and tracking initiation in HVDC bushing insulation under contaminated-surface conditions.
parsed.viable_reason: As written, the DC voltage-division relation and magnitude calculation are wrong (equal V/4 gives about 11.5 kV/mm, not 1.16 kV/mm, and DC division is conductivity-based), so the asserted reduction and validation threshold are unsupported.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Equipotential conductive grading screens/foils are conventional HV insulation measures, so applying them to reduce bushing radial field peaks would be obvious to a skilled engineer.
